problem: Confirmed approaching hand can leave the field of view while a forearm remains; missing landmarks alone do not prove withdrawal.
implementation: Confirmed-approach-gated local foreground retention, near-object removal comparison and a 3.5-second cap without a reliable owner hand; not arm semantics or physical contact sensing.
nativeReleaseBuild: passed arm64 and x86_64, executed arm64 only
privacy: 48x36 RGB signatures exist only in memory; no signatures/video in diagnostics or repository.

previousLiveLandmarkReplay.limitation: Unlabeled landmark replay does not establish live recall, false-positive rate or camera latency.

currentLiveAcceptance.status: passed final short trial by user
currentLiveAcceptance.limitation: No independently labeled action times or long-term false-positive rate. One recovery used the 3.5-second uncertainty cap; another used near-object change.

limitations: Foreground support alone cannot trigger the warning.
Similar colors, low contrast, body movement into the corridor and unavailable pre-approach background can affect retention.
New image feature extraction cannot be revalidated from old landmark-only recordings.
Long-duration accuracy, physical touch sensing, Intel hardware and older macOS are not validated.
Hand absent longer than 3.5 seconds without reliable hand geometry can dismiss the warning even if a forearm remains; this is a deliberate anti-latch tradeoff.

sensitivityCorrection.confirmation: Stable geometry can confirm across the existing multi-frame window instead of always waiting another camera frame.
sensitivityCorrection.negativeSweep: Typing-style articulation, lateral waving and static hand pass at low/default/high sensitivity.
